enumeratedValue.name: mode0
enumeratedValue.description: Frequency measurement performed with REF frequency > CUT Frequency.

enumeratedValue.name: mode1
enumeratedValue.description: Frequency measurement performed with REF frequency < CUT Frequency.

enumeratedValue.name: mode2
enumeratedValue.description: CUT period measurement performed.

enumeratedValue.name: mode3
enumeratedValue.description: Trigger based measurement performed. Note, each trigger pulse must be held for at least 2 ref_clk cycles.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG_START_POL0
enumeratedValue.description: Rising edge of TRIGGER[TRIG_START_SEL] will begin the measurement sequence.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG_START_POL1
enumeratedValue.description: Falling edge of TRIGGER[TRIG_START_SEL] will begin the measurement sequence.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG_END_POL0
enumeratedValue.description: Rising edge of TRIGER[TRIG_END_SEL] will end the measurement sequence.

enumeratedValue.name: TRIG_END_POL1
enumeratedValue.description: Falling edge of TRIGGER[TRIG_END_SEL] will end the measurement sequence.

enumeratedValue.name: SFA_TRIG_MEAS_EN0
enumeratedValue.description: The measurement will start by default with a dummy write to the REF and CUT counters.

enumeratedValue.name: SFA_TRIG_MEAS_EN1
enumeratedValue.description: The measurement will start after receiving a dummy write to the REF_CNT followed by receiving the trigger edge selected by TRIG_START_SEL and TRIG_START_POL.

enumeratedValue.name: SFA_IRQ_EN0
enumeratedValue.description: Interrupts are disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: SFA_IRQ_EN1
enumeratedValue.description: Interrupts are enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: SFA_EN0
enumeratedValue.description: The SFA is disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: SFA_EN1
enumeratedValue.description: The SFA is enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: MONITOR_EN0
enumeratedValue.description: Not in monitor mode .

enumeratedValue.name: MONITOR_EN1
enumeratedValue.description: In monitor mode.

field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: EXT
field.description: Contains extended (LOW word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: STD
field.description: Contains standard/extended (HIGH word) identifier of message buffer.

field.name: PRIO
field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE

field.description: Local priority. This 3-bit fieldis only used when LPRIO_EN bit is set in MCR and it only makes sense for Tx buffers. These bits are not transmitted. They are appended to the regular ID to define the transmission priority.

field.name: TIME_STAMP
field.description: Free-Running Counter Time stamp. This 16-bit field is a copy of the Free-Running Timer, captured for Tx and Rx frames at the time when the beginning of the Identifier field appears on the CAN bus.

field.name: DLC
field.description: Length of the data to be stored/transmitted.

field.name: RTR
field.description: Remote Transmission Request. One/zero for remote/data frame.

field.name: IDE
field.description: ID Extended. One/zero for extended/standard format frame.

field.name: SRR
field.description: Substitute Remote Request. Contains a fixed recessive bit.

field.name: CODE
field.description: Message Buffer Code. This 4-bit field can be accessed (read or write) by the CPU and by the FlexCAN module itself, as part of the message buffer matching and arbitration process.

field.name: ESI
field.description: Error State Indicator. This bit indicates if the transmitting node is error active or error passive.

field.name: BRS
field.description: Bit Rate Switch. This bit defines whether the bit rate is switched inside a CAN FD format frame.

field.name: EDL
field.description: Extended Data Length. This bit distinguishes between CAN format and CAN FD format frames. The EDL bit must not be set for Message Buffers configured to RANSWER with code field 0b1010.

enumeratedValue.name: zz236

enumeratedValue.name: zz237
enumeratedValue.description: DOUT based pattern. For READ operations only, DOUT of selected group will be latched in R_DATA. If more than one group is selected in R_ADR_CTRL[GRPSEL], the group with the lower index will be latched.

enumeratedValue.name: zz238
enumeratedValue.description: R_DATA based pattern. For READ operations, expected DOUT value of selected groups equals to R_DATA when XADR[0]==YADR[0] or ~R_DATA when XADR[0]!=YADR[0]. For PROG operations, DIN of selected groups equals R_DATA when XADR[0]==YADR[0] or ~R_DATA when XADR[0]!=YADR[0].

enumeratedValue.name: zz239
enumeratedValue.description: SCAN-IO pattern. For READ operations, control expected DOUT value of selected groups to SCAN-IO data pattern. For PROG operations, control DIN of selected groups to SCAN-IO data pattern.

enumeratedValue.name: zz240
enumeratedValue.description: REPAIR set. For PROG operation to IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2), R_REPAIR0_0 and R_REPAIR0_1 or R_REPAIR1_0 and R_REPAIR1_1 will control DIN. For READ operation on IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2), DOUT will be compared against R_REPAIR0_0 and R_REPAIR0_1 or R_REPAIR1_0 andR_REPAIR1_1. When this option is selected, only one flash block can be selected.

field.name: lbu2_use_refclk
field.description: Static bit set by FW based on Reference Clock Frequency. If reference clock frequency is lower and LBU can not support high baud rate of UART, then FW will set soc_use_ref_mode = 0. This is an indication for Bluetooth subsystem that there is some IP which need PLL to function which is LBU in this case.

field.name: btrtu1_use_ref_clk
field.description: Static bit set by FW. If it is required that timers need not be programmed with dynamic switching of T1/Reference, the BT_RTU1 source clock is set on reference clock so that the timer are not distrubed.

field.name: btrtu1_dbg_clk_ctrl
field.description: 1= Enable BT_RTU1 timers turn off during debugger mode 0= This feature is disabled

field.name: wd2_chip_rst_disable
field.description: 1: Disable the rtu2 watchdog reset to reset the chip 0: Enable

register.name: RFMCCFG
register.description: Radio Flash Memory Controller Configuration Register

enumeratedValue.name: CK_0
enumeratedValue.description: Normal configuration. When NBU CPU executes WFI and SLEEP_EN=1 (or if NBU CPU reset is asserted), and a sleep request from RFMC (LP_ENTER) NBU, MAN or WOR is asserted, the flash is put in low power, the sleep_rdy to RFMC asserts and the FRO will be disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: CK_1
enumeratedValue.description: Configuration where NBU, FRO and flash are not used. When NBU CPU reset is asserted, or NBU CPU executes WFI and SLEEP_EN=1, the flash will be placed in low power, the FRO disabled, the sleep_rdy to RFMC will assert and the NBU CM3 and AHB clocks will be gated off. The RF_CMC and NBU CPU will be without a clock until the next reset, but low power requests (RFMC LP_ENTER, MAN or WOR) will by accepted by RFMC since RF_CMC's sleep_rdy output will remain asserted.

enumeratedValue.name: CK_2
enumeratedValue.description: Configuration where NBU CPU is not used but FRO and flash can still be used. When NBU CPU reset is asserted, or NBU CPU executes WFI and SLEEP_EN=1, the clock to the NBU CPU will be gated. When RFMC (LP_ENTER), MAN or WOR request sleep, the flash is put in low power, the sleep_rdy to RFMC asserts and the FRO will be disabled as in configuration 00.

enumeratedValue.description: YADR decreased by 1 after first row. For READ operations only, YADR is decreased by 1 after XADR decreases to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: zz232
enumeratedValue.description: CKBD pattern. For READ operations only, compare DOUT with checkerboard data pattern for each read cycle.

enumeratedValue.name: zz233
enumeratedValue.description: ICKBD pattern. For READ operations only, compare DOUT with inverse checkerboard data pattern for each read cycle.

enumeratedValue.name: zz234
enumeratedValue.description: Diagonal pattern. Used for READ operations only, compare DOUT to diagonal pattern.

enumeratedValue.name: zz235
enumeratedValue.description: Fixed data pattern. For READ operations, comparison to DOUT for selected groups; refer to R_ADR_CTRL[GRPSEL] for modules with multiple groups.

enumeratedValue.name: zz236
enumeratedValue.description: Random data pattern which will be generated based on the initial seed set in R_DATA; for READ operations, used for DOUT comparison of selected groups. For PROG operations, used to control DIN of selected groups.

enumeratedValue.name: zz237
enumeratedValue.description: DOUT based pattern. For READ operations only, DOUT of selected group will be latched in R_DATA. If more than one group is selected in R_ADR_CTRL[GRPSEL], the group with the lower index will be latched.

enumeratedValue.name: zz238
enumeratedValue.description: R_DATA based pattern. For READ operations, expected DOUT value of selected groups equals to R_DATA when XADR[0]==YADR[0] or ~R_DATA when XADR[0]!=YADR[0]. For PROG operations, DIN of selected groups equals R_DATA when XADR[0]==YADR[0] or ~R_DATA when XADR[0]!=YADR[0].

enumeratedValue.name: zz239
enumeratedValue.description: SCAN-IO pattern. For READ operations, control expected DOUT value of selected groups to SCAN-IO data pattern. For PROG operations, control DIN of selected groups to SCAN-IO data pattern.

enumeratedValue.name: zz240
enumeratedValue.description: REPAIR set. For PROG operation to IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2), R_REPAIR0_0 and R_REPAIR0_1 or R_REPAIR1_0 and R_REPAIR1_1 will control DIN. For READ operation on IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2), DOUT will be compared against R_REPAIR0_0 and R_REPAIR0_1 or R_REPAIR1_0 andR_REPAIR1_1. When this option is selected, only one flash block can be selected.

enumeratedValue.name: zz241
enumeratedValue.description: REPAIR load. For READ operation only, DOUT from IFR1(7,1) and IFR1(7,2) is loaded to R_REPAIR0 and R_REPAIR1.

enumeratedValue.description: Expected data is compared to DOUT

field.name: WIN_FAD_WAIT_SYNCH
field.description: Time-window to wait for clean samples, before transitioning to AA search PHY state, if PD was found after antenna switch (referred to as T3 in the PHY state-machine section).

field.name: WIN_FAD_WAIT_PD
field.description: Time-window to wait for clean samples if PD was not found after antenna switch (referred to as T2 in the PHY state-machine section).

field.name: WIN_FAD_SEARCH_PD
field.description: Time-window to match preamble pattern on samples coming from the previously selected antenna (referred to as T1 in the PHY state-machine section).

field.name: WIN_SEARCH_PD
field.description: Time-window to match preamble pattern on samples coming from the currently selected antenna (referred to as T0 in the PHY state-machine section).

field.name: AA_FOUND

field.description: Indicates the hamming distance witnessed when AA match occurred.

field.name: CORR_MAX
field.description: Indicates the correlation witnessed when AA match occurred

field.name: TOF_OFF

enumeratedValue.description: 3 peaks;

field.description: AA correlator gain. Format ufix6en3. This gain is applied to soft bits from the demodulator before they are used for address search synchronization.

field.description: Hamming distance between the reference sequence and the Viterbi decoded received sequence

field.name: AA_FOUND
field.description: Indicates that a AA detect is active for both LR and uncoded.

field.name: CMAG_MAX
field.description: Indicates the maximum preamble correlation magnitude during preamble found

enumeratedValue.name: A1

enumeratedValue.name: A2
enumeratedValue.description: Use synch only (which may incorporate part of the preamble)

enumeratedValue.name: A3
enumeratedValue.description: Use mainly the sync detection: Use a low threshold on the preamble detector and launch the synch detection only if the preamble has shown a recent peak

field.name: GTSFREQ
field.description: Global timestamp frequency. Defines how often the ITM generates a global timestamp, based on the global timestamp clock frequency, or disables generation of global timestamps.

enumeratedValue.name: GTSFREQ_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disable generation of global timestamps.

enumeratedValue.name: GTSFREQ_1
enumeratedValue.description: Generate timestamp request whenever the ITM detects a change in global timestamp counter bits [47:7]. This is approximately every 128 cycles.

enumeratedValue.name: GTSFREQ_2
enumeratedValue.description: Generate timestamp request whenever the ITM detects a change in global timestamp counter bits [47:13]. This is approximately every 8192 cycles.

enumeratedValue.name: GTSFREQ_3
enumeratedValue.description: Generate a timestamp after every packet, if the output FIFO is empty.

enumeratedValue.name: BUSY_1

field.name: s8BIT

field.name: CYCCNTENA
field.description: CYCCNTENA bit. Enables CYCCNT. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOCYCCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCCNTENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCCNTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: POSTPRESET
field.description: POSTPRESET bits. Reload value for the POSTCNT counter. This field is UNK/SBZP if the NOCYCCNT bit is RAO.

field.name: POSTINIT
field.description: POSTINIT bits. Initial value for the POSTCNT counter. This field is UNK/SBZP if the NOCYCCNT bit is RAO.

field.name: CYCTAP
field.description: CYCTAP bit. Selects the position of the POSTCNT tap on the CYCCNT counter. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOCYCCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCTAP_0
enumeratedValue.description: POSTCNT tap at CYCCNT[6].

enumeratedValue.name: CYCTAP_1
enumeratedValue.description: POSTCNT tap at CYCCNT[10].

field.name: SYNCTAP
field.description: SYNCTAP bits. Selects the position of the synchronization packet counter tap on the CYCCNT counter. This determines the Synchronization packet rate.

enumeratedValue.name: SYNCTAP_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled. No Synchronization packets.

enumeratedValue.name: SYNCTAP_1
enumeratedValue.description: Synchronization counter tap at CYCCNT[24].

enumeratedValue.name: SYNCTAP_2
enumeratedValue.description: Synchronization counter tap at CYCCNT[26].

enumeratedValue.name: SYNCTAP_3
enumeratedValue.description: Synchronization counter tap at CYCCNT[28].

field.name: PCSAMPLENA
field.description: PCSAMPLENA bit. Enables use of POSTCNT counter as a timer for Periodic PC sample packet generation. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOTRCPKT bit is RAO or the NOCYCCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: PCSAMPLENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: No Periodic PC sample packets generated.

enumeratedValue.name: PCSAMPLENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Periodic PC sample packets generated.

field.name: EXCTRCENA
field.description: EXCTRCENA bit. Enables generation of exception trace. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOTRCPKT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCTRCENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCTRCENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: CPIEVTENA
field.description: CPIEVTENA bit. Enables generation of the CPI counter overflow event. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOPRFCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: CPIEVTENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: CPIEVTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: EXCEVTENA
field.description: EXCEVTENA bit. Enables generation of the Exception overhead counter overflow event. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOPRFCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCEVTENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCEVTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: SLEEPEVTENA
field.description: SLEEPEVTENA bit. Enables generation of the Sleep counter overflow event. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOPRFCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEPEVTENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEPEVTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: LSUEVTENA
field.description: LSUEVTENA bit. Enables generation of the LSU counter overflow event. This bit is UNK/SBZP if the NOPRFCNT bit is RAO.

enumeratedValue.name: LSUEVTENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: LSUEVTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: FOLDEVTENA

enumeratedValue.name: FOLDEVTENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: FOLDEVTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled.

field.name: CYCEVTENA

enumeratedValue.description: No POSTCNT underflow packets generated.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCEVTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: POSTCNT underflow packets generated, if PCSAMPLENA set to 0.

field.name: NOPFRCNT
field.description: NOPFRCNT bit. Shows whether the implementation supports the profiling counters.

enumeratedValue.name: NOPFRCNT_0
enumeratedValue.description: Supported.

enumeratedValue.name: NOPFRCNT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Not supported.

field.name: NOCYCCNT
field.description: NOCYCCNT bit. Shows whether the implementation supports a cycle counter.

enumeratedValue.name: NOCYCCNT_0
enumeratedValue.description: Cycle counter supported.

enumeratedValue.name: NOCYCCNT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Cycle counter not supported.

field.name: NOEXTTRIG
field.description: NOEXTRRIG bit. Shows whether the implementation includes external match signals, CMPMATCH[N].

enumeratedValue.name: NOEXTTRIG_0
enumeratedValue.description: CMPMATCH[N] supported.

enumeratedValue.name: NOEXTTRIG_1
enumeratedValue.description: CMPMATCH[N] not supported.

field.name: NOTRCPKT
field.description: NOTRCPKT bit. Shows whether the implementation supports trace sampling and exception tracing. If this bit is RAZ, the NOCYCCNT bit must also RAZ.

enumeratedValue.name: NOTRCPKT_0
enumeratedValue.description: Trace sampling and exception tracing supported.

enumeratedValue.name: NOTRCPKT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Trace sampling and exception tracing not supported.

field.name: NUMCOMP
field.description: NUMCOMP bits. Number of comparators implemented. A value of zero indicates no comparator support.

field.name: CYCCNT
field.description: CYCCNT[31:0]. Incrementing cycle counter value. When enabled, CYCCNT increments on each processor clock cycle. On overflow, CYCCNT wraps to zero.

field.name: CPICNT
field.description: CPICNT[7:0]. The base CPI counter. Counts additional cycles required to execute multi-cycle instructions, except those recorded by DWT_LSUCNT, and counts any instruction fetch stalls.

field.name: EXCCNT
field.description: EXCCNT[7:0]. The exception overhead counter. Counts the total cycles spent in exception processing.

field.name: SLEEPCNT
field.description: SLEEPCNT[7:0]. Sleep counter. Counts the total number of cycles that the processor is sleeping.

field.name: LSUCNT
field.description: LSUCNT[7:0]. Load-store counter. Increments on any additional cycles required to execute load or store instructions.

field.name: FOLDCNT
field.description: FOLDCNT[7:0]. Folded-instruction counter. Increments on each instruction that takes 0 cycles.

field.name: EIASAMPLE
field.description: EIASAMPLE[31:0]. Executed Instruction Address sample value.

field.name: MASK
field.description: MASK[4:0]. The size of the ignore mask, 0-31 bits, applied to address range matching. The maximum mask size is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED. A debugger can write 0b11111 to this field and then read the register back to determine the maximum mask size supported.

field.name: FUNCTION
field.description: FUNCTION[3:0]. Selects action taken on comparator match. This field resets to zero.

field.name: EMITRANGE
field.description: EMITRANGE bit. If the implementation supports trace sampling, enables generation of Data trace address offset packets, that hold Daddr[15:0]. If DWT_CTRL.NOTRCPKT is RAZ then this bit is UNK/SBZP.

enumeratedValue.name: EMITRANGE_0
enumeratedValue.description: Data trace address offset packets disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: EMITRANGE_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enable Data trace address offset packet generation.

field.name: CYCMATCH
field.description: CYCMATCH bit. If the implementation supports cycle counting, enable cycle count comparison for comparator 0. If DWT_CTRL.NOCYCCNT is RAZ then this bit is UNK/SBZP.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCMATCH_0
enumeratedValue.description: No comparison is performed.

enumeratedValue.name: CYCMATCH_1
enumeratedValue.description: Compare DWT_COMP0 with the cycle counter, DWT_CYCCNT.

field.name: DATAVMATCH
field.description: DATAVMATCH bit. Enables data value comparison, if supported. For comparator 0, when the CYCMATCH is set to 1, DATAVMATCH must be set to 0 for it to perform cycle count comparison. See LNK1ENA, DATAVSIZE, DATAVADDR0 and DATAVADDR1 for related information. If the implementation does not support data value comparison this bit is RAZ/WI.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVMATCH_0
enumeratedValue.description: Perform address comparison.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVMATCH_1
enumeratedValue.description: Perform data value comparison.

field.name: LNK1ENA
field.description: LNK1ENA bit. Indicates whether the implementation supports use of a second linked comparator. When LNK1ENA is RAO, the DATAVADDR1 field specifies the comparator to use as the second linked comparator.

enumeratedValue.name: LNK1ENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Second linked comparator not supported.

enumeratedValue.name: LNK1ENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Second linked comparator supported.

field.name: DATAVSIZE
field.description: DATAVSIZE[1:0]. For data value matching, specifies the size of the required data comparison.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVSIZE_0
enumeratedValue.description: Byte.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVSIZE_1
enumeratedValue.description: Halfword.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVSIZE_2
enumeratedValue.description: Word.

field.name: DATAVADDR0
field.description: DATAVADDR0[3:0]. When the DATAVMATCH bit is set to 1 this field can hold the comparator number of a comparator to use for linked address comparison. The DWT unit ignores the value of this field if the DATAVMATCH bit is set to 0.

field.name: DATAVADDR1
field.description: DATAVADDR1[3:0]. When the DATAVMATCH and LNK1ENA bits are both 1, this field can hold the comparator number of a second comparator to use for linked address comparison. The DWT unit ignores the value of this field unless the LNK1ENA bit is RAO and the DATAVMATCH bit is set to 1. If LNK1ENA is RAZ, this field is RAZ/WI.

field.name: MATCHED
field.description: MATCHED bit. Comparator match. A value of 1 indicates that the operation defined by the FUNCTION field occurred since the last read of the register. Reading the register clears this bit to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: MATCHED_0
enumeratedValue.description: No match.

field.name: MASK
field.description: MASK[4:0]. The size of the ignore mask, 0-31 bits, applied to address range matching. The maximum mask size is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED. A debugger can write 0b11111 to this field and then read the register back to determine the maximum mask size supported.

field.name: FUNCTION
field.description: FUNCTION[3:0]. Selects action taken on comparator match. This field resets to zero.

field.name: EMITRANGE
field.description: EMITRANGE bit. If the implementation supports trace sampling, enables generation of Data trace address offset packets, that hold Daddr[15:0]. If DWT_CTRL.NOTRCPKT is RAZ then this bit is UNK/SBZP.

enumeratedValue.name: EMITRANGE_0
enumeratedValue.description: Data trace address offset packets disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: EMITRANGE_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enable Data trace address offset packet generation.

field.name: DATAVMATCH
field.description: DATAVMATCH bit. Enables data value comparison, if supported. For comparator 0, when the CYCMATCH is set to 1, DATAVMATCH must be set to 0 for it to perform cycle count comparison. See LNK1ENA, DATAVSIZE, DATAVADDR0 and DATAVADDR1 for related information. If the implementation does not support data value comparison this bit is RAZ/WI.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVMATCH_0
enumeratedValue.description: Perform address comparison.

enumeratedValue.name: DATAVMATCH_1
enumeratedValue.description: Perform data value comparison.

field.name: LNK1ENA

enumeratedValue.name: LNK1ENA_0
enumeratedValue.description: Second linked comparator not supported.

enumeratedValue.name: LNK1ENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: Second linked comparator supported.

peripheral.name: FPB
peripheral.description: Flash Patch and Breakpoint Unit Registers

field.name: ENABLE
field.description: Enable bit for the FPB. A Power-on reset clears this bit to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_0
enumeratedValue.description: FPB disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_1
enumeratedValue.description: FPB enabled.

field.name: KEY
field.description: KEY bit. On any write to FP_CTRL, the FPB unit ignores the write unless this bit is 1. This bit is RAZ.

field.name: NUM_CODE_least
field.description: NUM_CODE[3:0]. The least significant bits of NUM_CODE, the number of instruction address comparators. If NUM_CODE[6:0] is zero, the implementation does not support any instruction address comparators.

field.name: NUM_LIT
field.description: NUM_LIT bits. The number of literal address comparators supported. If this field is zero, the implementation does not support literal comparators.

field.name: NUM_CODE_most
field.description: NUM_CODE[6:4]. The most significant bits of NUM_CODE, the number of instruction address comparators, see bits [7:4].

field.name: REMAP
field.description: REMAP bits. If the FPB supports flash patch remap, this field: - holds bits [28:5] of the base address in SRAM to which the FPB remaps the address - has an UNKNOWN value on reset. If the FPB only supports breakpoint functionality this field is UNK/SBZP.

field.name: RMPSPT
field.description: RMPSPT bit. Indicates whether the FPB unit supports flash patch remap.

enumeratedValue.name: RMPSPT_0
enumeratedValue.description: Remapping not supported. The FPB only supports breakpoint functionality.

enumeratedValue.name: RMPSPT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Hard-wired remap to SRAM region.

field.name: ENABLE
field.description: Enable bit for this comparator. A Power-on reset clears this bit to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_0
enumeratedValue.description: Comparator disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE_1
enumeratedValue.description: Comparator enabled.

field.name: COMP
field.description: COMP bits. Bits [28:2] of the address to compare with addresses from the Code memory region. Bits [31:29] and [1:0] of the address for comparison are zero. If a match occurs: - for an instruction address comparator, the REPLACE field defines the required action - for a literal address comparator, the FPB remaps the access. The reset value of this field is UNKNOWN.

field.name: REPLACE
field.description: REPLACE[1:0]. For an instruction address comparator: - Defines the behavior when the COMP address is matched. - The reset value of this field is UNKNOWN. For a literal address comparator: - Field is UNK/SBZP.

enumeratedValue.name: REPLACE_0
enumeratedValue.description: Remap to remap address.

enumeratedValue.name: REPLACE_1
enumeratedValue.description: Breakpoint on lower halfword, upper is unaffected.

enumeratedValue.name: REPLACE_2
enumeratedValue.description: Breakpoint on upper halfword, lower is unaffected.

enumeratedValue.name: REPLACE_3
enumeratedValue.description: Breakpoint on both lower and upper halfwords.

enumeratedValue.description: external clock

enumeratedValue.name: PROCESSOR_CLOCK
enumeratedValue.description: processor clock

field.name: COUNTFLAG
field.description: Returns 1 if timer counted to 0 since the last read of this register.

field.name: RELOAD
field.description: Value to load into the SysTick Current Value Register when the counter reaches 0

field.name: CURRENT
field.description: Reads current counter value at the time the register is accessed. Any write to the register clears the register to 0.

field.name: TENMS
field.description: Reload value to use for 10ms timing

field.name: SKEW
field.description: Indicates whether the TENMS value is exact

enumeratedValue.name: EXACT_VALUE
enumeratedValue.description: 10ms calibration value is exact

enumeratedValue.name: INEXACT_VALUE
enumeratedValue.description: 10ms calibration value is inexact, because of the clock frequency

field.name: NOREF
field.description: Indicates whether the device provides an alternative reference clock

enumeratedValue.name: CLOCK_DISABLED
enumeratedValue.description: The alternative reference clock is not provided

field.name: INTID
field.description: Interrupt ID of the interrupt to trigger, in the range 0-479.

register.name: AIRCR
register.description: Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register

field.name: VECTCLRACTIVE
field.description: Reserved for Debug use. This bit reads as 0. When writing to the register you must write 0 to this bit, otherwise behavior is UNPREDICTABLE. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SYSRESETREQ
field.description: System reset request. This bit allows software or a debugger to request a system reset. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW if SYSRESETREQS is 0. When SYSRESETREQS is set to 1, from Non-secure state this bit acts as RAZ/WI.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_REQUEST
enumeratedValue.description: Do not request a system reset.

enumeratedValue.name: REQUEST_RESET
enumeratedValue.description: Request a system reset.

field.name: SYSRESETREQS
field.description: System reset request, Secure state only. The value of this bit defines whether the SYSRESETREQ bit is functional for Non-secure use. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure State and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is available to both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is only available to Secure state.

field.name: PRIGROUP
field.description: Interrupt priority grouping field. This field determines the split of group priority from subpriority. This bit is banked between Security states

field.name: BFHFNMINS
field.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI Non-secure enable. The value of this bit defines whether BusFault and NMI exceptions are Non-secure, and whether exceptions target the Non-secure HardFault exception. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure-state and RO from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI are Secure.

enumeratedValue.name: NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault and NMI are Non-secure and exceptions can target Non-secure HardFault.

field.name: PRIS
field.description: Prioritize Secure exceptions. The value of this bit defines whether Secure exception priority boosting is enabled. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure state and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SAME_PRIORITY
enumeratedValue.description: Priority ranges of Secure and Non-secure exceptions are identical

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_PRIORITIZED
enumeratedValue.description: Non-secure exceptions are de-prioritized

field.name: ENDIANNESS
field.description: Data endianness bit. This bit is not banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: LITTLE_ENDIAN
enumeratedValue.description: Little-endian.

enumeratedValue.name: BIG_ENDIAN
enumeratedValue.description: Big-endian

field.name: VECTKEY
field.description: Register key: Reads as 0xFA05. On writes, write 0x5FA to VECTKEY, otherwise the write is ignored. This Field is not banked between Security states.

register.name: SCR
register.description: The SCR controls features of entry to and exit from low-power state.

field.name: SLEEPONEXIT
field.description: Indicates sleep-on-exit when returning from Handler mode to Thread mode. Setting this bit to 1 enables an interrupt driven application to avoid returning to an empty main application. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Do not sleep when returning to Thread mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Enter sleep, or deep sleep, on return from an ISR

field.name: SLEEPDEEP
field.description: Controls whether the processor uses sleep or deep sleep as its low-power mode. This bit is not banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Sleep.

enumeratedValue.name: DEEP_SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Deep sleep.

field.name: SLEEPDEEPS
field.description: Controls whether the SLEEPDEEP bit is only accessible from the Secure state. This bit in only accessible from the Secure state, and behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Nonsecure state. This bit is not banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit is accessible from both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Non-secure state.

field.name: SEVONPEND
field.description: Send Event on Pending bit. When an event or interrupt enters pending state, the event signal wakes up the processor from WFE. If the processor is not waiting for an event, the event is registered and affects the next WFE. The processor also wakes up on execution of an SEV instruction or an external event. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Only enabled interrupts or events can wakeup the processor, disabled interrupts are excluded.

enumeratedValue.name: INCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled events and all interrupts, including disabled interrupts, can wakeup the processor

register.name: SHCSR
register.description: System Handler Control and State Register

register.name: DHCSR_Read
register.description: Debug Halting Control and Status Register

field.name: C_DEBUGEN
field.description: Halting debug enable bit. If a debugger writes to DHCSR to change the value of this bit from 0 to 1, it must also write 0 to the C_MASKINTS bit, otherwise behavior is UNPREDICTABLE. This bit can only be set to 1 from the DAP, it cannot be set to 1 under software control. This bit is 0 after a Power-on reset.

enumeratedValue.name: C_DEBUGEN_0
enumeratedValue.description: Disabled

enumeratedValue.name: C_DEBUGEN_1
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled

field.name: C_HALT
field.description: Processor halt bit. This bit is UNKNOWN after a Power-on reset.

enumeratedValue.name: C_HALT_0
enumeratedValue.description: No effect.

enumeratedValue.name: C_HALT_1
enumeratedValue.description: Halt the processor.

field.name: C_STEP
field.description: Processor step bit. This bit is UNKNOWN after a Power-on reset.

enumeratedValue.name: C_STEP_0
enumeratedValue.description: No effect.

enumeratedValue.name: C_STEP_1
enumeratedValue.description: Step the processor.

field.name: C_MASKINTS
field.description: C_MASKINTS bit. When debug is enabled, the debugger can write to this bit to mask PendSV, SysTick and external configurable interrupts. The effect of any attempt to change the value of this bit is UNPREDICTABLE unless both: - before the write to DHCSR, the value of the C_HALT bit is 1. - the write to the DHCSR that changes the C_MASKINTS bit also writes 1 to the C_HALT bit. This means that a single write to DHCSR cannot set the C_HALT to 0 and change the value of the C_MASKINTS bit. The bit does not affect NMI. When DHCSR.C_DEBUGEN is set to 0, the value of this bit is UNKNOWN. This bit is UNKNOWN after a Power-on reset.

enumeratedValue.name: C_MASKINTS_0
enumeratedValue.description: Do not mask.

enumeratedValue.name: C_MASKINTS_1
enumeratedValue.description: Mask PenSV, SysTick and external configurable interrupts.

field.name: S_REGRDY
field.description: S_REGRDY bit. A handshake flag for transfers through the DCRDR: - Writing to DCRSR clears the bit to 0. - Completion of the DCRDR transfer then sets the bit to 1. This bit is valid only when the processor is in Debug state, otherwise the bit is UNKNOWN.

enumeratedValue.name: S_REGRDY_0
enumeratedValue.description: There has been a write to the DCRDR, but the transfer is not complete.

enumeratedValue.name: S_REGRDY_1
enumeratedValue.description: The transfer to or from the DCRDR is complete.

field.name: S_HALT
field.description: S_HALT bit. Indicates whether the processor is in Debug state.

enumeratedValue.name: S_HALT_0
enumeratedValue.description: Not in Debug state.

enumeratedValue.name: S_HALT_1
enumeratedValue.description: In Debug state.

field.name: S_SLEEP
field.description: S_SLEEP bit. Indicates whether the processor is sleeping. The debugger must set the C_HALT bit to 1 to gain control, or wait for an interrupt or other wakeup event to wakeup the system.

enumeratedValue.name: S_SLEEP_0
enumeratedValue.description: Not sleeping.

enumeratedValue.name: S_SLEEP_1
enumeratedValue.description: Sleeping.

field.name: S_LOCKUP
field.description: S_LOCKUP bit. Indicates whether the processor is locked up because of an unrecoverable exception. This bit can only be read as 1 by a remote debugger, using the DAP. The value of 1 indicates that the processor is running but locked up. The bit clears to 0 when the processor enters Debug state.

enumeratedValue.name: S_LOCKUP_0
enumeratedValue.description: Not locked up

enumeratedValue.name: S_LOCKUP_1
enumeratedValue.description: Locked up

field.name: S_RETIRE_ST
field.description: S_RETIRE_ST bit. Indicates whether the processor has completed the execution of an instruction since the last read of DHCSR. This is a sticky bit, that clears to 0 on a read of DHCSR. A debugger can check this bit to determine if the processor is stalled on a load, store or fetch access. This bit is UNKNOWN after a Power-on or Local reset, but then is set to 1 as soon as the processor executes and retires an instruction.

enumeratedValue.name: S_RETIRE_ST_0
enumeratedValue.description: No instruction retired since last DHCSR read.

enumeratedValue.name: S_RETIRE_ST_1
enumeratedValue.description: At least one instruction retired since last DHCSR read.

field.name: S_RESET_ST
field.description: S_RESET_ST bit. Indicates whether the processor has been reset since the last read of DHCSR. This is a sticky bit, that clears to 0 on a read of DHCSR.

enumeratedValue.name: S_RESET_ST_0
enumeratedValue.description: No reset since last DHCSR read.

enumeratedValue.name: S_RESET_ST_1
enumeratedValue.description: At least one reset since last DHCSR read.

field.name: REGSEL

field.name: VC_CORERESET
field.description: VC_CORERESET bit. Enable Reset Vector Catch. This causes a Local reset to halt a running system. If DHCSR.C_DEBUGEN is set to 0, the processor ignores the value of this bit.

enumeratedValue.description: Reset Vector Catch disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: VC_CORERESET_1
enumeratedValue.description: Reset Vector Catch enabled.

field.name: VC_HARDERR
field.description: VC_HARDERR bit. Enable halting debug trap on a HardFault exception. If DHCSR.C_DEBUGEN is set to 0, the processor ignores the value of this bit.

enumeratedValue.name: VC_HARDERR_0
enumeratedValue.description: Halting debug trap disabled.

enumeratedValue.name: VC_HARDERR_1
enumeratedValue.description: Halting debug trap enabled.

enumeratedValue.name: DWTENA_0

enumeratedValue.name: DWTENA_1
enumeratedValue.description: DWT enabled.

field.name: SWIDTH
field.description: SWIDTH[N] represents a trace port width of (N+1). The meaning of each bit is: 0 = Width (N+1) not supported. 1 = Width (N+1) supported.

field.name: CWIDTH
field.description: CWIDTH[N] represents a trace port width of (N+1). The meaning of each bit is: 0 = Width (N+1) is not the current trace port width. 1 = Width (N+1) is the current trace port width.

field.name: TXMODE

enumeratedValue.description: Parallel trace port mode.

enumeratedValue.name: TXMODE_1
enumeratedValue.description: Asynchronous SWO, using Manchester encoding.

enumeratedValue.name: TXMODE_2
enumeratedValue.description: Asynchronous SWO, using NRZ encoding.

field.name: CycCount

field.name: CLAIMSET
field.description: A bit programmable register bank which sets the Claim Tag Value. Write 1 to set the bit in the claim tag. A read will return a logic 1 for all implemented locations.

field.name: CLAIMCLR

field.name: NumberOfTraceInputs
field.description: Number of trace inputs. Specifies the number of trace inputs: b000000 = 1 input b000001 = 2 inputs If your implementation includes an ETM, the value of this field is b000001.

field.name: TRACECELKIN
field.description: Asynchronous TRACECLKIN. Specifies whether TRACECLKIN can be asynchronous to CLK.

enumeratedValue.name: TRACECELKIN_1
enumeratedValue.description: b1 = TRACECLKIN can be asynchronous to CLK

field.name: MinimumBufferSize
field.description: Minimum buffer size. Specifies the minimum TPIU buffer size: b010 = 4 bytes

field.name: TraceAndClockModes
field.description: Trace and clock modes. This bit Reads-As-Zero (RAZ), indicating that tracedata and clock modes are supported.

enumeratedValue.name: TraceAndClockModes_1
enumeratedValue.description: Not supported

field.name: ETMPD
field.description: ETM power down. This bit can be used by an implementation to control if the ETM is in a low power state. This bit must be cleared by the trace software tools at the beginning of a debug session. When this bit is set to 1, writes to some registers and fields might be ignored.

field.name: PS
field.description: Port size. The ETM-M4 has no influence over the external pins used for trace. These bits are implemented but not used. On an ETM reset these bits reset to 0b001.

field.name: SP
field.description: Stall processor. The FIFOFULL output can be used to stall the processor to prevent overflow. The FIFOFULL output is only enabled when the stall processor bit is set to 1. When the bit is 0 the FIFOFULL output remains LOW at all times and the FIFO overflows if there are too many trace packets. Trace resumes without corruption once the FIFO has drained, if overflow does occur. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

field.name: BO
field.description: Branch output. When set to 1 all branch addresses are output, even if the branch was because of a direct branch instruction. Setting this bit enables reconstruction of the program flow without having access to the memory image of the code being executed. When this bit is set to 1, more trace data is generated, and this may affect the performance of the trace system. Information about the execution of a branch is traced regardless of the state of this bit. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

field.name: DRC
field.description: Debug request control. When set to 1 and the trigger event occurs, the DBGRQ output is asserted until DBGACK is observed. This enables the ARM processor to be forced into Debug state. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

field.name: ETMP
field.description: ETM programming. This bit must be set to 1 at the start of the ETM programming sequence. Tracing is prevented while this bit is set to 1. On an ETM reset this bit is set to b1.

field.name: ETMPS
field.description: ETM port selection. This bit can be used to control other trace components in an implementation. This bit must be set by the trace software tools to ensure that trace output is enabled from this ETM. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: ETMPS_0
enumeratedValue.description: ETMEN is LOW.

enumeratedValue.name: ETMPS_1
enumeratedValue.description: ETMEN is HIGH.

field.name: PM2
field.description: This bit is implemented but has no function. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

field.name: PM
field.description: These bits are implemented but have no function. An ETM reset sets these bits to 0.

field.name: PS3
field.description: This bit is implemented but has no function. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

field.name: TE
field.description: When set, this bit enables timestamping. An ETM reset sets this bit to 0.

field.name: NumberOfAddressComparatorPairs
field.description: Number of address comparator pairs. The value of these bits is b0000, indicating that address comparator pairs are not implemented.

field.name: NDVC
field.description: Number of data value comparators. The value of these bits is b0000, indicating that data value comparators are not implemented.

field.name: NMMD
field.description: Number of memory map decoders. The value of these bits is b00000, indicating that memory map decoder inputs are not implemented.

field.name: NC
field.description: Number of counters. The value of these bits is b001, indicating that one counter is implemented.

field.name: SP
field.description: Sequencer present. The value of this bit is 0, indicating that the sequencer is not implemented.

field.name: NEI
field.description: Number of external inputs. The value of these bits is between b000 and b010, indicating the number of external inputs, from 0 to 2, implemented in the system.

field.name: NEO
field.description: Number of external outputs. The value of these bits is b000, indicating that no external outputs are supported.

field.name: FFLP
field.description: FIFOFULL logic present. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that FIFOFULL logic is present in the ETM. To use FIFOFULL the system must also support the function, as indicated by bit [8] of ETMSCR.

field.name: NCIDC
field.description: Number of Context ID comparators. The value of these bits is b00, indicating that Context ID comparators are not implemented.

field.name: TSSBP
field.description: Trace start/stop block present. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that the Trace start/stop block is present.

field.name: CMA
field.description: Coprocessor and memory access. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that memory-mapped access to registers is supported.

field.name: ETMIDRP
field.description: The value of this bit is 1, indicating that the ETMIDR, register 0x79, is present and defines the ETM architecture version in use.

field.name: UOF
field.description: Untraced overflow flag. If set to 1, there is an overflow that has not yet been traced. This bit is cleared to 0 when either: - trace is restarted - the ETM Power Down bit, bit [0] of the ETM Control Register, 0x00, is set to 1. Note: Setting or clearing the ETM programming bit does not cause this bit to be cleared to 0.

field.name: Progbit
field.description: ETM programming bit value (Progbit). The current effective value of the ETM Programming bit (ETM Control Register bit [10]). Tou must wait for this bit to go to 1 before you start to program the ETM.

field.name: Status
field.description: Holds the current status of the trace start/stop resource. If set to 1, it indicates that a trace on address has been matched, without a corresponding trace off address match.

field.name: Trigger
field.description: Trigger bit. Set when the trigger occurs, and prevents the trigger from being output until the ETM is next programmed.

field.name: MaximumPortSize
field.description: Maximum ETM port size bits [2:0]. These bits are used in conjunction with bit [9]. The value of these bits is b001.

field.name: FIFOFULLsupported
field.description: FIFOFULL supported. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that FIFOFULL is supported. This bit is used in conjunction with bit [23] of the ETMCCR.

field.name: MaximumPortSize3
field.description: Maximum ETM port size bit [3]. This bit is used in conjunction with bits [2:0]. Its value is 0. This has no effect on the TPIU trace port.

field.name: PortSizeSupported
field.description: Port size supported. This bit reads as 1 if the currently selected port size is supported. This has no effect on the TPIU trace port.

field.name: PortModeSupported
field.description: Port mode supported. This bit reads as 1 if the currently selected port mode is supported. This has no effect on the TPIU trace port.

field.name: N
field.description: These bits give the number of supported processors minus 1. The value of these bits is b000, indicating that there is only one processor connected.

field.name: NoFetchComparisons
field.description: No Fetch comparisons. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that fetch comparisons are not implemented.

field.name: TraceControlEnable
field.description: Trace start/stop enable. The trace start/stop resource, resource 0x5F, is unaffected by the value of this bit.

enumeratedValue.name: TraceControlEnable_0
enumeratedValue.description: Tracing is unaffected by the trace start/stop logic.

enumeratedValue.name: TraceControlEnable_1
enumeratedValue.description: Tracing is controlled by the trace on and off addresses configured for the trace start/stop logic.

field.name: FIFOFullLevel
field.description: FIFO full level. The number of bytes left in FIFO, below which the FIFOFULL or SupressData signal is asserted. For example, setting this value to 15 causes data trace suppression or processor stalling, if enabled, when there are less than 15 free bytes in the FIFO.

field.name: ImplementationRevision
field.description: Implementation revision. The value of these bits is b0000, indicating implementation revision, 0.

field.name: MinorETMarchitectureVersion
field.description: Minor ETM architecture version. The value of these bits is 0b0101, indicating minor architecture version number 5.

field.name: MajorETMarchitectureVersion
field.description: Major ETM architecture version. The value of these bits is 0b0010, indicating major architecture version number 3, ETMv3.

field.name: ProcessorFamily
field.description: Processor family. The value of these bits is 0b1111, indicating that the processor family is not identified in this register.

field.name: LoadPCfirst
field.description: Load PC first. The value of this bit is 0, indicating that data tracing is not supported.

field.name: ThumbInstructionTracing
field.description: 32-bit Thumb instruction tracing. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that a 32-bit Thumb instruction is traced as a single instruction.

enumeratedValue.name: ThumbInstructionTracing_0
enumeratedValue.description: A 32-bit Thumb instruction is traced as two instructions, and exceptions might occur between these two instructions.

enumeratedValue.name: ThumbInstructionTracing_1
enumeratedValue.description: A 32-bit Thimb instruction is traced as a single instruction.

field.name: SecurityExtensionSupport
field.description: Security Extensions support. The value of this bit is 0, indicating that the ETM behaves as if the processor is in Secure state at all times.

enumeratedValue.name: SecurityExtensionSupport_0
enumeratedValue.description: The ETM behaves as if the processor is in Secure state at all times.

enumeratedValue.name: SecurityExtensionSupport_1
enumeratedValue.description: The ARM architecture Security Extensions are implemented by the processor.

field.name: BranchPacketEncoding
field.description: Branch packet encoding. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that alternative branch packet encoding is implemented.

enumeratedValue.name: BranchPacketEncoding_0
enumeratedValue.description: The ETM implements the original branch packet encoding.

enumeratedValue.name: BranchPacketEncoding_1
enumeratedValue.description: The ETM implements the alternative branch packet encoding.

field.name: ImplementorCode
field.description: Implementor code. These bits identify ARM as the implementor of the processor. The value of these bits is 01000001.

field.name: ExtendedExternalInputSelectors
field.description: Extended external input selectors. The value of these bits is 0, indicating that extended external input selectors are not implemented.

field.name: ExtendedExternalInputBus
field.description: Extended external input bus. The value of these bits is 0, indicating that the extended external input bus is not implemented.

field.name: ReadableRegisters
field.description: Readable registers. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that all registers are readable.

field.name: DataAddressComparisons
field.description: Data address comparisons. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that data address comparisons are not supported.

field.name: InstrumentationResources
field.description: Instrumentation resources. The value of these bits is 0b000, indicating that no Instrumentation resources are supported.

field.name: EmbeddedICEwatchpointInputs
field.description: EmbeddedICE watchpoint inputs. The value of these bits is 0b0100, indicating that the number of EmbeddedICE watchpoint inputs implemented is four. These inputs come from the DWT.

field.name: TraceStartStopBlockUsesEmbeddedICEwatchpointInputs
field.description: Trace Start/Stop block uses EmbeddedICE watchpoint inputs. The value of this bit is 1, indicating that the Trace Start/Stop block uses the EmbeddedICE watchpoint inputs.

field.name: EmbeddedICEbehaviorControlImplemented
field.description: EmbeddedICE behavior control implemented. The value of this bit is 0, indicating that the ETMEIBCR is not implemented.

field.name: TimestampingImplemented
field.description: Timestamping implemented. This bit is set to 1, indicating that timestamping is implemented.

field.name: ReducedFunctionCounter
field.description: Reduced function counter. Set to 1 to indicate that Counter 1 is a reduced function counter.

field.name: TimestampEncoding
field.description: Timestamp encoding. Set to 1 to indicate that the timestamp is encoded as a natural binary number.

field.name: TimestampSize
field.description: Timestamp size. Set to 0 to indicate a size of 48 bits.

field.name: StartResourceSelection
field.description: Start resource selection. Setting any of these bits to 1 selects the corresponding EmbeddedICE watchpoint input as a TraceEnable start resource. Bit [0] corresponds to input 1, bit [1] corresponds to input 2, bit [2] corresponds to input 3, and bit [3] corresponds to input 4.

field.name: StopResourceSelection
field.description: Stop resource selection. Setting any of these bits to 1 selects the corresponding EmbeddedICE watchpoint input as a TraceEnable stop resource. Bit [16] corresponds to input 1, bit [17] corresponds to input 2, bit [18] corresponds to input 3, and bit [19] corresponds to input 4.

field.name: TraceID
field.description: Trace ID to output onto the trace bus. On an ETM reset this field is cleared to 0x00.

field.name: ETMpoweredup
field.description: The value of this bit indicates whether you can access the ETM Trace Registers. The value of this bit is always 1, indicating that the ETM Trace Registers can be accessed.

field.name: EXTIN
field.description: A read of these bits returns the value of the EXTIN[1:0] input pins.

field.name: COREHALT

field.name: TRIGGER
field.description: A write to this bit sets the TRIGGER output.
